newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to increase 1997 T-bill volumes.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to increase 1997 T-bill volumes.

text.p: Ukraine will increase issues of Treasury bills this year to 8.0 billion hryvnias from a previously forecast 6.0 billion hryvnias, the government press service said in a statement on Thursday.
Annual T-bill issue volumes were set at 2.5 billion hryvnias but increased to 3.5 billion in March and 6.0 billion in May.
The government also plans to issue domestic debt this year worth one billion hryvnias.
In 1996 Ukraine issued about 3.3 billion of hryvnias in T-bills. At the most recent auction on July 8 yields on six-, nine- and 12-month paper fell to 19.64, 27.81 and 30.34 percent respectively.
The economy ministry says the finance ministry earned 4.38 billion hryvnias in the first six months for budget coffers.
Foreign investors attracted by slower inflation and relatively high yields have become major buyers of the bills.
This year's budget foresees financing some of the deficit with T-bill revenues. Expenditures were set at 28.12 billion hryvnias and revenues at 22.4 billion hryvnias.
Inflation has been forecast at 25 percent in budget papers compared to 39.7 percent in 1996, but recently officials have said it will be about 17 percent.
